name: Meridian-Swell
description: Meridian-Swell is a small ocean moon locked in the embrace of its gas giant parent, one hemisphere forever turned toward a sky-filling banded colossus. A single warm meridian circles the moon where tidal flexing keeps the sea liquid, a ring of steaming dark water between ice fields on either side. In the low gravity, waves move with dreamlike slowness, great glassy swells that take minutes to rise and fall.

The air is thin but breathable, carrying a mineral tang from the vent fields that steam along the warm meridian. Sound behaves oddly here; the slow swells lap against the ice in long, bell-like tones that resonate for kilometers. When the parent gas giant crosses the sky, its reflected glow turns the whole sea copper, and every shadow on the ice doubles.

Beneath the ice, a subterranean ocean connects the warm belt to the dark side, and microbial mats thrive around the geothermal vents, tinting the shallows rust and jade. The automated beacon standing on the meridian's largest floe predates current settlement—it broadcasts a simple navigation tone, but its power source is of no human design and has never needed refueling. Whoever placed it wanted ships to keep coming here safely.

Research consortiums prize Meridian-Swell's extremophile compounds, and its position makes it an ideal waypoint for traffic skirting the gas giant's radiation belts. But the beacon's tone shifted by a single note last year—detected by exactly one passing freighter—and the consortium's charter quietly forbids discussing it. On the far hemisphere, facing away from everything, fresh cracks have begun spreading through ice that surveys say should be solid.
